label: Inter-peak 13:00-14:00
time: seconds after midnight (same clock and window as traffic_<period>.bin)

fields.path: lane indices into road_network lanes[] in driving order (internal lanes of each connection included)
fields.enter: time each path element is entered (s)
fields.leave: time the last element is left (null: still on it at t1)
fields.jumps: [i, t]: element i-1 left at t, not drawn until enter[i] (teleport or outside the exported network)
fields.changes: path indices entered by a lateral lane change (no connection)
fields.stops: bus stops: element, position along its lane shape (m), arrive, depart
fields.end_pos: with leave null: distance along the last lane at t1 (FCD)

lane_choice: Per vehicle, a dynamic programme over the lanes of each route edge that permit its vClass minimises lane changes: consecutive lanes joined by a SUMO connection cost 0 (the connection's via chain of internal lanes is inserted), a lane change at the start of the next edge costs 1 (listed in changes), one on the previous edge as well 2; ties are broken by a per-vehicle SHA-1 hash of the lane ids, spreading traffic over equivalent lanes. A bus uses its stop lane on edges with a stop. Elements outside the exported road network are dropped (jumps).
timing: Edge entry times are SUMO's (vehroute-output exit times: departure, then the exit time of the previous edge); mesoscopic SUMO has no internal edges, so the internal lanes of a connection get min(length / internal lane speed, the time at the edge's mean speed over edge + internal lengths) taken from the end of the edge before it; the normal lane gets the rest. Mesoscopic exit times are whole seconds: where an element would be passed faster than 1.3 x its speed limit (often in 0 s), its entry is moved earlier, taking the time from the elements before it (entries_moved and max_entry_shift_s in provenance). Constant speed within each element; buses hold at their stop position from started to ended (stops). jumps [i, t]: element i-1 was left at t (jam teleport or leaving the exported domain) and element i is entered at enter[i] without motion in between. leave is null for vehicles still on their last element at the end of the simulation; end_pos (m along that lane, from FCD at t1) is reached at constant speed from its entry.

provenance.source: SUMO vehroute-output (exit-times, write-unfinished), stop-output started/ended in the route output, teleport warnings of the SUMO log
provenance.vehicles: every vehicle on an exported lane during [t0, t1]; elements trimmed to the window
